what: The plan changes the SKILL.md public flag allowlist but leaves an exact structural pin that will fail when --manual is inserted
scenario_or_breakage: After SKILL.md changes from `--brainstorm`, `--no-dedup`, and `--run-id` to include `--manual`, `bash scripts/relevant-checks.sh` fails even though the implementation is otherwise correct
suggested_fix: Promote scripts/test-design-structure.sh to UPDATED and add pins for argument-hint, allowlist order, flag-table row, write-run-params invocation, recovery merge, flags.md bullet, and approval-gates auto/manual branch

what: Top-level approval-gate contract still says no reviewer suggestion is ever auto-applied and the user is always prompted
scenario_or_breakage: The proposed Gate B default contradicts the loaded contract before the new Gate B subsection is reached, giving the orchestrator two normative instructions in the same file
suggested_fix: Rewrite the header contract as dual-mode: Gate A and Gate C always prompt; Gate B prompts only in manual mode and otherwise auto-applies accepted in-scope findings

what: Gate A re-entry prose says plan modification authority remains with Gate B's user choices and explicitly applied findings
scenario_or_breakage: In default mode, Gate B has no user choice before plan mutation, so a Gate B(c)/Gate C(b) re-entry after auto-apply would be described by stale manual-only semantics
suggested_fix: Update the Gate A re-entry paragraph to distinguish default auto-applied Gate B revisions from manual-mode user-approved revisions, and keep the no-mutation claim scoped to Gate A itself

what: The public skill catalog is not in the files-to-modify list even though it enumerates /design flags and behavior

suggested_fix: Add docs/skills.md to UPDATED and include --manual / -m in the arguments line plus a short note that it restores the Gate B prompt

what: The post-PR blocker command names add-blocked-by.sh without the real path, while the /block-issue wrapper uses a different positional interface
